issues.description: Element: Animal constructor and accessors (Animal(String), getName(), setName()). Problem statement: the UML and explicit text require these members to have protected visibility (UML shows '#' for the Animal constructor and getters/setters and the text in the tasks explicitly asks for protected getter/setter). Solution repository: Animal.java implements a public constructor (public Animal(String)) and public getName()/setName() methods. This mismatch between the specified protected visibility and the solution's public visibility can confuse students about intended encapsulation and may cause automated checks that expect protected visibility to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the visibility mismatch by aligning implementation with the problem statement. Option A (preferred to match the exercise text): change Animal.java so the constructor and accessors use protected visibility: 'protected Animal(String name)', 'protected String getName()', and 'protected void setName(String newName)'. Update any code in the solution that accesses these members accordingly (subclasses can still call them). Option B (if public was intended): update the problem statement UML and the textual instructions to state that the constructor, getName(), and setName() are public so that specification and implementation match.
